Subject: SIG questionnaire and evidence packaging for Redwood evaluation

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. FinSet's security and procurement teams are kicking off the vendor assurance review for our Q1 platform rollout. Attached is our SIG questionnaire (we converted to XLSX for internal review) — would you be able to provide: 1) a control mapping (SIG question -> Redwood control / evidence filename), 2) a short artifact packet per control (PDFs or exportable logs), and 3) a proposed delivery cadence?

Specific asks:
- We prefer a single zip with clearly named artifacts; a CSV control map works best for our intake tool.
- We will need KMS/HSM attestations (we cannot accept private key material).
- Our procurement lead (procurement@finset.com) will pick up on pricing/PO later this month.

Can you confirm feasibility and a short plan? We aim to complete the compliance review by 2028-12-08.

Thanks,
Sarah Murray
Sr. Vendor Assurance Manager | FinSet Financial

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire and evidence packaging for Redwood evaluation

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the questionnaire. We can definitely support the requested deliverables. Proposed approach (high level):

1) Intake & map (2 business days): Ben will map each SIG item to Redwood controls and reference artifacts in a CSV (format compatible with your intake tool).
2) Artifact curation (3–5 business days): Soojin will assemble technical artifacts (architecture diagrams, attestation PDFs, log extracts). We will redact any customer-specific data.
3) HSM/KMS provenance (2 business days): We cannot share private keys; we will provide KMS key provenance, HSM attestation PDFs, and relevant KMS rotation logs.
4) Delivery & follow-up (1 day): Deliver zip bundle, control_map.csv, and a short readme. We'll also schedule a 30-min walkthrough.

Timeline: if we start Monday (2028-11-15) we can deliver an initial packet by 2028-11-20 and finalize by 2028-11-22. Let us know if you need an earlier slot.

Attachments we'll include in the first packet (examples): redwood_control_map_20281115.csv, kv_hsm_key_provenance_20281115.pdf, service-architecture-kv-cache.pdf.

Proposed owners:
- Ben Carter: control mapping + compliance QA
- Soojin Lee: technical artifacts, logs, attestation prep
- Lauren Bishop (me): primary contact + intake coordination

If that works, I'll start the mapping and share the CSV draft. Also, can you confirm how you prefer SAML metadata (URL or file)?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

- Two items require a short architecture note (KV cache multi-tenant isolation) — attached diagram included.
- KMS items: provide key rotation logs + HSM attestation PDF; we must explicitly state we will not provide private key material.

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-16T14:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control map draft and artifact index (technical clarifications)

Quick technical clarifications for artifacts we will provide to FinSet:

- KMS/HSM: we'll provide kv_hsm_key_provenance_20281115.pdf which contains:
  * HSM vendor attestation (certified FIPS level),
  * key provenance and rotation timestamps (redacted to remove customer IDs),
  * KMS access control lists and role-based access screenshots.
- Logs: rotation and KMS access logs will be exported as CSV excerpts (last 90 days). We will redact requestor ARNs that include customer account numbers.
- SAML / SSO: we can publish our metadata file (redwood_saml_metadata.xml) or provide an endpoint URL. For FinSet's automation, the file may be easier.
- Architectural diagram: service-architecture-kv-cache.pdf includes component boundaries and data flow with caching and KV-cache eviction notes.

Note: For any item that could expose tenant identifiers, we'll provide a sanitized excerpt and include a readme that explains what was redacted and why.

I'll assemble the first artifact bundle and share a link by EOD 2028-11-20.

— Soojin
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
